title: Kast's 'New State Architecture' Commission Draws Cross-Party Fire Over Exclusion of Communist Party and Frente Amplio
detail: The 12-member Comisión Nueva Arquitectura del Estado — unveiled August 25 to spend 120 days proposing a leaner ministerial structure (Chile grew from 18 to 25 ministries in recent decades) — drew mounting criticism August 26 for excluding the Communist Party (PC) and Frente Amplio (FA), Boric's governing coalition parties, despite including figures from RN, UDI, Republicanos, Christian Democracy, PPD and the Socialist Party. PC president Lautaro Carmona called the omission 'anticomunismo' and said his party would form its own parallel body; Frente Amplio's Karina Oliva (Maipú mayor) and party figures echoed the complaint, arguing PC/FA governing experience was directly relevant to state redesign. Even Chile Vamos figure Evelyn Matthei urged the government not to 'forget the left' in a reform meant to outlast one administration. Partido de la Gente deputy Zandra Parisi separately noted her party's 14 deputies were also left out despite holding votes the reform will eventually need in Congress.
